liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Morning Dew and The Other One leading into Wharf Rat are singled out as worth the download alone [12]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Not Fade Away goes into Goin' Down the Road and back to Not Fade Away, followed by Johnny B. Goode, after Good Lovin' [10]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 review): Played at an extremely fast pace, according to this listener [10]

## The recordings

- **gd71-02-23.sbd.orf.113.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 173 min; rated 4.64/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Mix takes a while to settle; then Bill and Phil are prominent, Jerry's guitar sits back, and everything is clear [9]
- **gd1971-02-23.sbd.miller.110353.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 172 min; rated 4.33/5 by 12 [2]
- **gd1971-02-23.sbd.evans-waddell.GEMS.82755.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 164 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: Removing the tone makes a noticeable sound difference; the transfer is speed-matched to the circulating source [3]
- **gd1971-02-23.151503.aud.partial.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: audience recording; 12 songs; 86 min [4]. Said about its sound: Some tracks were rebalanced to bring Jerry's guitar up in the mix [4]

## Around the show

- Venue was a funky little theater with bench seats, often freezing in winter, in a working-class suburb about 20 miles from New York City [8]
- Drinking age in Port Chester was 18 during this week-long run [9]
- Lineup described: Jerry on a Les Paul, Bobby on a 335, Phil on an SG, and Ron playing Hammond B-3 organ [18]
- Show listed as an E.S.P. show with NRPS as another act; disc changes are seamless [2]
- Like much of early 1971, the band played tight and dirty during this run of shows [8]
- Sound on this winter run is much clearer than the 1970 shows at the Capitol [9]
- Reviewer says this show has a different feeling from the other five shows in the run [12]
- Several songs claimed as first-time played had already been played earlier, starting with 18 Feb at the same venue [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-02-23.sbd.miller.110353.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD [2]. Also: Uploader calls this a huge upgrade over all circulating copies and says it is not the Betty source [2]
- **gd1971-02-23.sbd.evans-waddell.GEMS.82755.flac16**: taped by DAT from the collection of Todd Evans; transferred by Editing and Mastering in Wavelab6.0 and Ozone. Dithered L2type1ultra by Jamie Waddell; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7 inch reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) [3]. Also: Upgrade of earlier source: the ringing tone present in shnid 113 was removed without noise reduction software; Reel flips occur in Bobby McGee and at the end of Wharf Rat; digital glitches patched in Me and My Uncle and Good Lovin' [3]
- **gd1971-02-23.151503.aud.partial.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: taped by Unknown; transferred by SIRMick & Matt Vernon; source: Unknown aud (3rd gen cassette) - From the collection of Doug Lamarre [4]. Also: Partial audience recording with pitch adjustments; gain surges smoothed out during two songs [4]
